Both screenshots are visually identical, and odiff confirms 0 differing pixels (exit code 0). The clone is complete and pixel-perfect at the default 1280×900 viewport.

## Summary

This was a minimal, unstyled page (no `<style>` tags or stylesheet links at all — everything visible is pure browser UA-default rendering), so the work centered on two things:

**Componentization decision:** red-twine flagged `li.slide` as a repeating fragment (confidence 0.85, 2 occurrences). Reading the actual content confirmed they're genuinely the same kind of thing (product slide items), so I kept them as one repeated pattern rather than treating the match as coincidental.

**JS-gated content, handled by reading the source, not guessing:** The raw HTML has only 2 `<li class="slide">` items, but a small inline script clones both and appends them with `aria-hidden="true"`, simulating a slick-carousel-style infinite loop (per the script's own comment). Since the entire transform was visible and legible directly in a small inline `<script>` block, I copied that script verbatim into the clone rather than needing slowcure to diff pre/post-JS states — the source already fully explained the DOM mutation.

**Styling approach:** windtailor on `body` and on `#slides > li.slide` confirmed there are zero custom tokens beyond browser defaults — 8px body margin, 32px/700 h1, default list markup — plus one very minor minted token (`text-32` for the h1 size). Since Tailwind's preflight reset would strip exactly the UA defaults this page relies on (list bullets, base margins), I loaded Tailwind via CDN with `corePlugins.preflight: false` and added the single measured token, rather than fighting the reset to reconstruct defaults that were already correct un-touched.

**Unrecreatable/out of scope:** `product-1.jpg`/`product-2.jpg` are referenced via root-relative paths with no live host (this is a local fixture), so per the hotlink-only rule I left them exactly as authored rather than inventing a host or placeholder — both original and clone show the same broken-image state.

**Fidelity check:** Screenshotted both at the same pinned 1280×900 viewport (`original.png`, `clone-round1.png`, `diff-round1.png`, all in the run's temp dir) and ran odiff: **0 changed pixels, exit code 0** — a pixel-perfect match on the first round, so no further iteration was needed.
